newsitem.title: LUXEMBOURG: Court upholds Commission olive oil test rules.
newsitem.headline: Court upholds Commission olive oil test rules.

text.p: The European Court of First Instance rejected on Friday a bid for damages from an Italian olive oil merchant, Oleifici, against the European Commission.
Oleifici argued the Commission's regulation on testing olive oil and olive oil residue failed to provide for a transitional period, causing Oleifici to lose 7,345 million LIT in product and costs.

Oleifici found itself with tonnes of Tunisian olive oil it could not immediately sell, and placed the oil in a customs warehouse in April, 1992. In May the Commission's regulation came into effect and Oleifici could not sell that oil in the Community because it no longer satisfied testing criteria.
The court rejected arguments from Oleifici that the Commission's failure to act failed tests of legal certainty, proportionality, discrimination and a violation of rights.

ayant pour objet une demande de reparation du prejudice pretendument subi par la requerante du fait de l'absence de mesure transitoire dans le reglement (CEE) no 1429/92 de la Commission, modifiant le reglement (CEE) no 2568/91 relatif aux caracteristiques des huiles d'olive et de grignons d'olive ainsi qu'aux methodes d'analyse y afferentes (JO L 150, p. 17)
2. La requerante est condamnee aux depens.
